23: # Forgejo operations — backup, restore, upgrades
24: 
25: ## Overview
26: 
27: Day-to-day operations for a self-hosted Forgejo instance: consistent backups
28: with `forgejo dump` (or snapshotting), safe upgrades between releases, and
29: restore/verification. Forgejo follows semantic versioning since 7.0.0, and the
30: database stores its schema version so a downgrade is refused automatically.
31: 
32: ## Details
33: 
34: ### Backup
35: 
36: The reliable option is a synchronized point-in-time snapshot of all storage
37: Forgejo uses. On k3s that means snapshotting the Longhorn volume
38: (`./02_Knowledge/technologies/kubernetes/longhorn/storage.md`); if storage is
39: spread across several systems (DB on one volume, repos on another), stop
40: Forgejo during the backup so the pieces stay consistent.
41: 
42: For a simple single-filesystem setup the built-in command is:
43: 
44: ```bash
45: forgejo dump
46: ```
47: 
48: - Produces a single zip containing configuration, repositories, and the
49:   database.
50: - SQLite is already included in the zip; for PostgreSQL/MySQL also take a
51:   native `pg_dump`/`mysqldump` — the SQL dump embedded by `forgejo dump` has
52:   known bugs when re-injected into a new database.
53: - Schedule it as a k8s CronJob writing to a backup location (e.g. a separate
54:   volume or object storage), keeping a few rotations.
55: 
56: ### Restore
57: 
58: 1. Stop Forgejo.
59: 2. Extract the dump zip and restore data, repos, and config to the data volume.
60: 3. Restore the native database dump (for Postgres/MySQL).
61: 4. Start Forgejo and verify:
62:    `forgejo doctor check --all --log-file /tmp/doctor.log`
63:    plus a manual web-UI walk-through (login, a repo, an issue).
64: 
65: ### Upgrades
66: 
67: Forgejo release lifecycle:
68: 
69: | Channel | Support |
70: |---|---|
71: | **Stable** (latest) | Bugfix + security fixes for ~3 months + 2-week overlap |
72: | **LTS** (version published the first quarter of every year) | Critical fixes for ~1 year 3 months |
73: | **Experimental** (dev) | Not for production |
74: 
75: Upgrade procedure:
76: 
77: 1. **Back up first** — required when moving across a stable release, wise for
78:    minor/patch.
79: 2. Read the release notes for the target version, including known problematic
80:    upgrade paths (see the upgrade guide).
81: 3. Before switching: `forgejo manager flush-queues` (queued data is not
82:    guaranteed compatible between versions).
83: 4. Perform the upgrade by replacing the container image or binary — migrations
84:    run automatically on first start.
85: 5. **Verify carefully**: `forgejo doctor check --all` plus a manual checklist.
86:    A restore after an upgrade is easy; fixing a live instance weeks later is not.
87: 
88: Notes:
89: 
90: - Major version jumps (e.g. 15 → 16) may contain breaking changes and require
91:   the manual procedure; upgrading X → X+1 needs human verification. Staying on
92:   the `16` image tag gives minor updates automatically.
93: - Docker installs need docker >= 20.10.6.
94: - The database version guard refuses to start a downgraded binary against a
95:   newer database — do not bypass it.
96: - Subscribe to the security-announcements repo to plan security releases.
97: 
98: ### Day-to-day
99: 
100: - Logs: k8s — `kubectl logs -f deploy/forgejo -n forgejo`; Forgejo can also
101:   write logs to files via `[log]` sections (console/file modes); SQL logging
102:   is toggled by `LOG_SQL=true` in the `[database]` section.
103: - Health: rely on pod liveness/readiness probes hitting the web port; run
104:   `forgejo doctor` after any upgrade.
105: - Cross-check storage usage on the Longhorn PVC periodically.
106: 
107: ## Sources / Further Reading
108: 
109: - Upgrade guide: https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/admin/upgrade/
110: - CLI reference (`dump`, `doctor`, `forgejo-cli`): https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/admin/command-line/
111: - Release schedule: https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/admin/release-schedule/
112: - Logging configuration: https://forgejo.org/docs/latest/admin/troubleshooting/logging/
113: - Install: `./02_Knowledge/technologies/services/forgejo/install-config.md`

27: 
28: ## Overview
29: 
30: Forgejo is a community-run fork of Gitea developed under the Codeberg e.V.
31: umbrella — a soft-fork in 2022 that became a hard-fork in early 2024. It is a
32: lightweight, self-hosted Git forge that provides repository hosting plus issue
33: tracking, pull requests, a package registry, and GitHub-Actions-style CI. It
34: runs as a single Go application
35: with a small resource footprint, which makes it a natural fit for a homelab
36: that wants private Git hosting without a SaaS dependency.
37: 
38: ## Details
39: 
40: ### Why self-host Git hosting
41: 
42: - **Privacy and control**: repositories, issues, and CI stay on local hardware.
43: - **No SaaS dependency**: no vendor lock-in, rate limits, or per-user cost.
44: - **Homelab-scale footprint**: a single binary plus a database (SQLite is
45:   enough for a personal instance) keeps the resource cost low.
46: 
47: ### Feature surface
48: 
49: - Repositories with protected branches, tags, and releases
50: - Issue tracking, labels, milestones, projects, and wiki
51: - Pull requests and reviews with merge-message and PR templates
52: - Package registry (container, npm, PyPI, Go, Maven, and more)
53: - Forgejo Actions — GitHub-Actions-style CI executed by `forgejo-runner`
54: - Repository mirrors (pull/push), webhooks, and an OAuth2 provider
55: - Fine-grained access tokens, 2FA, and instance moderation tools
56: 
57: ### Architecture
58: 
59: ```
60: ┌──────────┐   HTTPS   ┌──────────┐   port 3000   ┌────────────────────┐
61: │ Traefik  │ ────────► │ Forgejo  │ ────────────► │ SQLite / PostgreSQL │
62: │ (ingress)│           │ (web +   │   git over    │ / MySQL            │
63: └──────────┘           │  git)    │   SSH/HTTP    └────────────────────┘
64:                        └──────────┘       │
65:                               Longhorn PVC │  (repos + data)
66:                                            ▼
67:                                   ┌──────────────────┐
68:                                   │ forgejo-runner(s) │  ← Forgejo Actions
69:                                   └──────────────────┘
70: ```
71: 
72: - The web UI, git HTTP endpoints, and the git SSH server all come from the
73:   single Forgejo process; a reverse proxy (Traefik in this homelab) terminates
74:   TLS in front of it.
75: - Supported databases: SQLite (default), PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB.
76: - Repository data lives on the filesystem — in k3s, a Longhorn PVC

80:

83:   bump (e.g. 15 → 16) may contain breaking changes.

93:   in the pipeline; see `./02_Knowledge/technologies/services/forgejo/install-config.md`.

19: # Migrating repositories to Forgejo
20: 
21: ## Overview
22: 
23: Repositories can be brought into Forgejo either as a **one-shot migration** (a
24: copy of the code plus issues, PRs, and releases) or as a **mirror** (kept in
25: sync with the source). One-shot migrations and pull mirrors start from the web
26: UI's migration flow; push mirrors are configured per-repository. Migrations
27: and mirrors work with GitHub, Gitea, GitLab, Gogs, and plain URLs. Migration
28: is how a homelab
29: instance adopts an existing GitHub/Gitea history instead of starting from an
30: empty repo.
31: 
32: ## Details
33: 
34: ### One-shot migration
35: 
36: - Go to **Create → New Migration** and pick the source:
37:   GitHub, Gitea, GitLab, Gogs, or a generic git URL.
38: - Authenticate with a token (see `./02_Knowledge/technologies/services/forgejo/security.md`
39:   for fine-grained token scopes) — for GitHub, docs recommend a fine-grained
40:   personal access token with Content read.
41: - Choose what to bring over: repository itself, issues, pull requests, releases,
42:   milestones, labels, wiki. PR/issue comments are filtered according to the
43:   selected migration options.
44: - Migration runs server-side; for large or LFS-heavy repositories the `[git]`
45:   timeout settings (config cheat sheet) may need raising.
46: 
47: ### Mirrors (continuous sync)
48: 
49: - A **pull mirror** re-fetches the source repository on a schedule
50:   (default `[mirror]` interval), keeping code, branches, and tags in sync.
51: - A **push mirror** pushes a Forgejo repo to a remote (e.g. GitHub) — by
52:   default it uses `git push --mirror` (all branches and tags); an optional
53:   branch filter restricts which branches are pushed. This is useful when
54:   Forgejo is canonical but an external copy is still published.
55: - Pull mirroring is chosen at repository creation (New Migration + the 'This
56:   repository will be a mirror' checkbox); push mirrors are set in **Settings →
57:   Repository → Mirror Settings**.
58: - A repository cannot be converted into a pull mirror after creation, and a
59:   push mirror force-pushes — it overwrites any changes on the remote.
60: 
61: ### Practical migration checklist
62: 
63: - **Tokens first**: generate a scoped token on the source and a Forgejo access
64:   token for API/CLI work afterwards.
65: - **LFS / large files**: verify Git LFS content transfers; LFS objects are not
66:   mirrored over SSH push mirrors. If the source blocks it, clone + push the
67:   LFS objects manually.
68: - **Wiki and packages**: not every source migrates these cleanly — move them
69:   separately (export/import) if needed.
70: - **Releases and tags**: confirm tags arrive; a re-tag can be done from a local
71:   clone if the migration missed some.
72: - **Old URLs**: GitHub mirrors may be kept alive; or add DNS/web redirects so
73:   existing links still resolve.
74: - **Users and orgs**: repo-level migrations bring author names/commits as-is;
75:   account/org structure is recreated on Forgejo manually.
76:

78:

80: two-step path: any Gitea ≤ v1.22.x → Forgejo v10.0.x, then v10.0.x → any newer
81: Forgejo (e.g. v16). This is an instance upgrade, not a repo migration — see the
82: upgrade guide's from-Gitea section and `./02_Knowledge/technologies/services/forgejo/operations.md`.

# Command-line interface

Forgejo comes with a command-line interface (CLI) for administrative actions. It is documented below and is not to be confused with user CLIs that can be used to [interact with a Forgejo instance](https://delightful.coding.social/delightful-forgejo/#command-line).

## forgejo `--help`[](#forgejo---help)

```
NAME:
   forgejo - Beyond coding. We forge.

USAGE:
   forgejo [global options] [command [command options]]


DESCRIPTION:
   By default, forgejo will start serving using the web-server with no argument, which can alternatively be run by running the subcommand "web".

COMMANDS:
   help, h          Shows a list of commands or help for one command
   web              Start the Forgejo web server
   serv             (internal) Should only be called by SSH shell
   hook             (internal) Should only be called by Git

   dump             Dump Forgejo files and database

   migrate          Migrate the database

   migrate-storage  Migrate the storage
   dump-repo        Dump the repository from git/github/gitea/gitlab
   restore-repo     Restore the repository from disk
   actions          Manage Forgejo Actions
   cert             Generate self-signed certificate
   generate         Generate Forgejo's secrets/keys/tokens
   forgejo-cli      Forgejo CLI

GLOBAL OPTIONS:
   --version, -v                    print the version
   --help, -h                       show help
   --custom-path string, -C string  Set custom path (defaults to '{WorkPath}/custom')
   --config string, -c string       Set custom config file (defaults to '{WorkPath}/custom/conf/app.ini')
   --work-path string, -w string    Set Forgejo's working path (defaults to the directory of the Forgejo binary)

# Command-line interface

Forgejo comes with a command-line interface (CLI) for administrative actions. It is documented below and is not to be confused with user CLIs that can be used to [interact with a Forgejo instance](https://delightful.coding.social/delightful-forgejo/#command-line).

## forgejo `--help`[](#forgejo---help)

```
NAME:
   forgejo - Beyond coding. We forge.

USAGE:
   forgejo [global options] [command [command options]]


DESCRIPTION:
   By default, forgejo will start serving using the web-server with no argument, which can alternatively be run by running the subcommand "web".

COMMANDS:
   help, h          Shows a list of commands or help for one command
   web              Start the Forgejo web server
   serv             (internal) Should only be called by SSH shell
   hook             (internal) Should only be called by Git
   keys             (internal) Should only be called by SSH server
   dump             Dump Forgejo files and database
   admin            Perform common administrative operations
   migrate          Migrate the database
   doctor           Diagnose and optionally fix problems, convert or re-create database tables
   manager          Manage the running forgejo process
   embedded         Extract embedded resources
   migrate-storage  Migrate the storage
   dump-repo        Dump the repository from git/github/gitea/gitlab
   restore-repo     Restore the repository from disk
   actions          Manage Forgejo Actions
   cert             Generate self-signed certificate
   generate         Generate Forgejo's secrets/keys/tokens
   forgejo-cli      Forgejo CLI

GLOBAL OPTIONS:
   --version, -v                    print the version
   --help, -h                       show help
   --custom-path string, -C string  Set custom path (defaults to '{WorkPath}/custom')
   --config string, -c string       Set custom config file (defaults to '{WorkPath}/custom/conf/app.ini')
   --work-path string, -w string    Set Forgejo's working path (defaults to the directory of the Forgejo binary)
   --help, -h                       show help
   --version, -v                    print the version
```

### admin user create-authorized-integration[](#admin-user-create-authorized-integration)

```
NAME:
   forgejo admin user create-authorized-integration

USAGE:
   forgejo admin user create-authorized-integration [options]

DESCRIPTION:
   Creates an authorized integration. Authorized integrations allow Forgejo to
   receive JWTs from external sources, validate their claims against
   user-defined rules, and grant access to Forgejo's API on behalf of a user.

   The issuer may be set to "urn:forgejo:authorized-integrations:actions"
   to support JWTs from the local instance's Forgejo Actions, utilizing the
   enable-openid-connect flag in a workflow.

OPTIONS:
   --help, -h                                                       show help
   --custom-path string, -C string                                  Set custom path (defaults to '{WorkPath}/custom')
   --config string, -c string                                       Set custom config file (defaults to '{WorkPath}/custom/conf/app.ini')
   --work-path string, -w string                                    Set Forgejo's working path (defaults to the directory of the Forgejo binary)
   --username string, -u string                                     Username
   --name string                                                    Name of the authorized integration for later identification
   --description string                                             Optional description for the authorized integration
   --issuer string                                                  JWT issuer ('iss' claim), example: https://forgejo.example.org/api/actions
   --claim-eq string=string [ --claim-eq string=string ]            Zero-or-more claim equality checks, formatted as claim=value, example: "actor=someuser"
   --claim-in string=string [ --claim-in string=string ]            Zero-or-more claim equality in list checks, formatted as claim=value1,value2,... example: "actor=user1,user2"
   --claim-glob string=string [ --claim-glob string=string ]        Zero-or-more claim glob checks, formatted as claim=value, example: "sub=repo:forgejo/*:pull_request"
   --claim-glob-in string=string [ --claim-glob-in string=string ]  Zero-or-more claim glob in list checks, formatted as claim=va*ue1,va*ue2,... example: "sub=repo:*/*:pull_request,repo:*/*:refs:*"
   --scope string [ --scope string ]                                One-or-more scopes to apply to access token, examples: "all", "read:issue", "write:repository" (default: "all")
   --repo string [ --repo string ]                                  Zero-or-more specific repositories that can be accessed, or "all" to allow access to all repositories, example: "owner1/repo1" (default: "all")
   --help, -h                                                       show help

GLOBAL OPTIONS:
   --custom-path string, -C string  Set custom path (defaults to '{WorkPath}/custom')
   --config string, -c string       Set custom config file (defaults to '{WorkPath}/custom/conf/app.ini')
   --work-path string, -w string    Set Forgejo's working path (defaults to the directory of the Forgejo binary)
```
